original_question: For the noncommutative algebra C^infinity_prop(G_FN, |T G_N|^{1/2}) associated with the linearized foliation on the conormal bundle of a Riemannian foliation, can one define a notion of noncommutative Hamiltonian flow such that the transverse Hamiltonian flows constructed from homogeneous degree-one Hamiltonians become examples of noncommutative Hamiltonian flows?
target_in_paper: Problem 4.6 in Section 4.4 (“Noncommutative symplectic geometry”): define a notion of noncommutative Hamiltonian flow on a noncommutative algebra so that the transverse Hamiltonian flows on C^infty_prop(G_FN, |T G_N|^{1/2}) are examples. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601093))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right algebra C^infty_prop(G_FN, |T G_N|^{1/2}), the linearized foliation FN on the conormal bundle N^*F of a Riemannian foliation, and the paper’s goal of making the transverse Hamiltonian flows into examples of a general notion of noncommutative Hamiltonian flow. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601093))
missing_details: The paper’s setup is a compact foliated manifold (M,F); the specific algebra and Poisson-structure discussion here require F to be Riemannian. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601093))

The algebra is not just any noncommutative algebra but the complex involutive algebra of properly supported smooth half-densities on G_FN, where “properly supported” means that the range map restricted to the support is proper over tilde N^*F. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601093))

Problem 4.6 is asked in the immediate context of a noncommutative Poisson structure in the sense of Xu / Block–Getzler: a Hochschild 2-cocycle P with P∘P a Hochschild 3-coboundary, and this context is omitted in the draft. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601093))

The phrase “transverse Hamiltonian flows” refers specifically to Definition 4.1, namely the one-parameter group F_t^* of automorphisms of C^infty_prop(G_FN, |T G_N|^{1/2}) induced by a flow F_t on G_FN. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601093))

The Hamiltonian p must satisfy the paper’s exact hypotheses: p is homogeneous of degree 1, defined on a conic neighborhood of tilde N^*F = N^*F minus the zero section inside tilde T^*M = T^*M minus the zero section, and its restriction to tilde N^*F is constant along the leaves of FN. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601093))

To build F_t^*, one chooses an extension tilde p in S^1(tilde T^*M) agreeing with p near tilde N^*F; its Hamiltonian flow preserves tilde N^*F and FN and induces the flow F_t on G_FN, and Definition 4.1 is independent of the choice of tilde p. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601093))

For full paper-faithfulness, the quantifier should be universal: the requested notion should make every transverse Hamiltonian flow arising from such a p into a noncommutative Hamiltonian flow, not merely some examples chosen ad hoc. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601093))

The paper phrases the problem slightly more generally than the draft: first define the notion on a noncommutative algebra, and then require the above flows on C^infty_prop(G_FN, |T G_N|^{1/2}) to fall under that notion. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601093))
refined_question: Let (M,F) be a compact Riemannian foliated manifold, let FN be the linearized foliation on the conormal bundle N^*F, let G_FN be its holonomy groupoid, and let A = C^infty_prop(G_FN, |T G_N|^{1/2}) be the involutive algebra of properly supported smooth half-densities on G_FN, equipped with the natural noncommutative Poisson structure arising from the Block–Getzler construction for the transversally symplectic foliation FN. Can one define a notion of Hamiltonian flow for a noncommutative algebra with such a Poisson structure so that, for every function p homogeneous of degree 1 on a conic neighborhood of tilde N^*F in tilde T^*M whose restriction to tilde N^*F is constant along the leaves of FN, the one-parameter group F_t^* of automorphisms of A induced by the transverse Hamiltonian flow of p in the sense of Definition 4.1 is a noncommutative Hamiltonian flow?
justification: The draft is targeting the open problem stated explicitly as Problem 4.6, not any of the early-section statements. It is already close to the official wording, but the paper’s actual intent is only fully visible after combining Section 2.3 (the algebra C^infty_prop(G_FN, |T G_N|^{1/2}) as the noncommutative cotangent bundle), Section 4.1 / Definition 4.1 (what “transverse Hamiltonian flow” means and the exact hypotheses on p), Section 3.1 (the notation tilde N^*F = N^*F minus the zero section), and Section 4.4 (the surrounding noncommutative Poisson-geometry framework and Problem 4.6 itself). The refined question keeps exactly that scope and does not broaden the paper’s problem beyond what is stated there. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601093))
